name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Reflex Splice — 'Razorwake'
description:
The Arcturus Reflex Splice is a combat-grade neuromuscular augmentation system that intercepts motor signals between the spinal cord and peripheral musculature, inserting a synthetic relay cluster — the ADR-7 node — at the T1–T4 vertebral junctions. This relay pre-processes threat response signals using a dedicated threat-assessment microprocessor, effectively bypassing the brain's slower conscious processing loop for a predefined set of physical responses. The result is a reaction time reduction of approximately 140 milliseconds for trained motor programs, which in close-quarters combat represents the difference between a block and a broken arm.

What distinguishes Razorwake from cheaper reflex boosters is its trained-response architecture. The system does not simply accelerate all movement — it must be calibrated to a specific operator's existing combat muscle memory over a 6-week conditioning protocol. This makes it deeply personal equipment; a Razorwake splice pulled from one operator and installed in another will fire responses that may be actively harmful, triggering the previous user's combat patterns in a new body. Arcturus Defense Solutions has built significant revenue around recalibration services as a result. The ADR-7 node also features an optional 'hot mode' that can be toggled via subvocal command, entering a higher-gain state that extends pre-processing to offensive strike initiation — at the cost of fine motor control and a significant metabolic burn.

Razorwake was originally developed under an Arcturus contract for special operations units in the Meridian Enforcement Compact, and military-spec units still carry Arcturus serial numbers traceable to that program. Civilian and black-market variants have proliferated through decommissioned operators selling their calibrated units — a practice Arcturus officially discourages while quietly providing recalibration services to whoever walks through the door.

cultural_context: In Meridian 88's street-combat culture, a Razorwake splice is a serious credential. The visible ADR-7 node — detectable as a slight ridge along the upper back when shirtless — is recognized by anyone with combat experience as a marker of professional violence. It is not flashy in the way chrome limbs or optical implants are flashy; it is the quiet signal of someone who has invested in being harder to kill. Among corporate security, it is standard issue for close-protection teams. Among independent operators, owning one indicates either a military background or the resources to purchase at Tier 2, both of which command respect.

story_hooks: A decommissioned Razorwake unit surfaces on the black market still calibrated to a Meridian Enforcement operator who is officially listed as killed in action three years ago — but the calibration was updated six months ago.

A player character's splice begins misfiring during stress, triggering responses from a previous owner's combat memory — violent, specific responses that suggest the previous owner did things the current owner doesn't want to be doing.

Arcturus Defense Solutions is recalling a batch of ADR-7 nodes citing a 'firmware irregularity' — but the recall notice only went to corporate clients, not the black-market chain. The irregularity causes hot mode to not disengage.
An arena fighter with a Razorwake splice is losing matches they should win — someone has been accessing the ADR-7's calibration remotely, slowly degrading their patterns to set up a fixed fight.
